q: How does an alumina refinery at Renukoot count CO2 from its steam and calciners?
title: Renukoot alumina refinery: steam CO2
short: Count coal burnt for steam used in digestion and fuel burnt in calciners, from tonnes or kilolitres with heating value and carbon content, per tonne of alumina. Alumina is not a CBAM good, but it is the largest bought input in an aluminium buyer's full footprint.
audience: Alumina refineries in Sonbhadra and the smelters they supply

ul: Coal or gas for steam in Bayer digestion.
Fuel oil or gas in calciners.
Caustic soda and lime bought in, upstream.

p: If the refinery feeds your own smelter, it is your Scope 1. Report it as its own line so the alumina figure can be checked.
Smelters buying alumina put it in Scope 3, category 1. CBAM leaves it out.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel, electricity and freight invoices into a dated, fingerprinted record per site, so each figure you send a buyer traces back to the documents behind it.
